proposition: Sarf studies word-internal form (root, pattern, derivation); nahw studies sentence-level function (case, government, roles).
rationale: matches the repo's own layering (sarf decides form BEFORE nahw decides contextual function) but the proposition itself is instructional framing, not a checkable rule

proposition: Every Arabic word is built from a root placed into a pattern.
rationale: false as stated: particles, primitive nouns, many proper nouns and loanwords have no productive root-pattern derivation; the repo treats rootlessness as a taught category (particles are 'rootless, taught never blank')

proposition: Words sharing a root are related in meaning (taught via a same-root word family; family members not reproduced here — clean-room boundary).
rationale: overgeneralization OG-1: root-sharing NEVER implies entry identity, shared lexeme, shared sense or shared translation (controlling repo invariant); semantic kinship is a tendency, not a licence

proposition: إِنَّ and its sisters make the following noun accusative (ismuha) while the predicate stays nominative (khabaruha).
rationale: standard paradigm-level grammar consistent with the dependency-lattice enum (inna_family governor_family), but NO fixture bank exercises abrogator government (crosswalk xn-04); per-occurrence application always needs the iʿrāb two-vote gate

proposition: كَانَ and its sisters keep their subject nominative and make the predicate accusative.
rationale: same posture as cl-004 (kana_family enum exists, no fixture bank)

proposition: لَمْ governs the jussive and negates the PAST; لَنْ governs the subjunctive and negates the future.
rationale: agrees with nahw/rules/negation-rules.json and the skill's negation procedure, but that rules file has zero executable consumer (GAP-N2)

overgeneralization OG-3 risk: مَا (p099) is negation OR relative OR interrogative OR masdariyyah by context; the lesson's scoped statement is true only inside its verbal-negation frame; one meaning of مَا never applies globally

proposition: Diptotes (الممنوع من الصرف) reject tanwin and take fatha for the genitive.
rationale: the companion lesson L4.M4.02 itself restores full declension when the diptote is definite or in idafa — the L4.M4.01 statement alone over-applies; the pilot's diptote awareness (jarr=fatha on لِءَادَمَ) matches the RESTORED-declension-aware rule

proposition: الَّذِي/الَّتِي agree with the antecedent in gender and number, and the relative clause carries a resumptive pronoun (عائد).
rationale: consistent with p094/p095/p097 entry family; no executable relative-clause checker exists in the repo

source_ref.section: theory of governance — Basran vs Kufan disputes on العامل

proposition: Certain governance analyses differ between the Kufan and Basran schools (L6.M4 presents disputes; L6.M1 is rhetoric/prosody, not school disputes).
rationale: school-dependent analyses must be recorded as attributed alternatives, never resolved by vote or preference; the repo routes genuine disputes to scholar/arbitration rows

proposition: A pattern learned from lesson sentences may be applied to any matching surface elsewhere (implicit in the curriculum's practice model).
rationale: the programme's location-first doctrine: surface match NEVER authorizes reuse; per-occurrence evidence and certification govern projection; lesson-derived patterns reach occurrences only as guarded analogous candidates

proposition: A vocabulary-table gloss is the word's translation (implicit in the vocabulary-table method; rows not reproduced).
rationale: overgeneralization OG-5: a dictionary gloss does not determine translation at an occurrence; sense selection is contextual (nahw) and Qamus-entry-governed; vocabulary rows are recall aids only

proposition: أَنْ، لَنْ، كَيْ govern the subjunctive (fatha on the imperfect).
rationale: paradigm-true; per-occurrence, أَنْ (p013) collides with إِنْ/أَنَّ/إِنَّ under weak keys — the state-transition forbidden table covers this but is not machine-enforced (GAP-N3)

source_ref.section: Form-I active participle فاعل (passive مفعول is L2.M4.02)

proposition: فَاعِل forms the Form-I active participle; مَفْعُول the passive participle.
rationale: matches sarf/rules/verb-measures.json paradigm slots (the one genuinely consumed Store A file); a per-token wazn classifier still does not exist (113-row derivative bank unconsumed)

proposition: The م of a place-noun on pattern مَفْعِل/مَفْعَل is a pattern augment, not a root letter (pilot demonstrates on the independently selected standard example مَسْجِد, root س ج د).
rationale: correct letter-ownership analysis matching sarf@2.4's candidate letter-ownership direction; promoted to a full candidate procedure + fixtures in curriculum/l1l6/pilot/ with clean-room examples (no lesson-distinctive words); stays candidate until owner adjudication
